attribution.note: Zitron's own summarising sentence ('In essence'), drawing on the Goldman/Janous material but asserted in his voice. Only the attribution of 'forgotten how to do' goes to Janous.

semantics.note: Adding 'growth' is a fair gloss on 'requires'. This is a present-tense observation about an infrastructure requirement, worded emphatically.

contract.note: Reading 'totally rebuild' as comprehensive reconstruction is literal and ordinary, though the phrase may be hyperbole for massive expansion. The contract flags this, and the result depends on which reading is used. The quarter used as the observation period is inferred.

evidence.note: EPRI scenarios (May 2024) put all data centers at 4.6–9.1% of US electricity by 2030 and mention regional supply challenges. This covers all data centers, not generative AI alone, and neither shows nor rules out a national rebuild.

reviews.rationale: The only item is a contemporary EPRI scenario release showing large data-center demand growth and regional strain. It gives no grid-wide engineering requirement and does not separate generative AI demand, so it meets neither the support nor the contradiction condition. The packet does not settle the claim.

semantics.note: 'I see no situation where' is firm, unhedged expectation, so this is a scored forecast. The proposition keeps the causal mechanism (backers stop subsidising compute) and the open 'at some point' horizon.

contract.note: Requiring withdrawal of support that causes both firms to stop LLM development matches the words. Saying that renewals do not disprove an indefinite forecast is fair. 'Cloud compute welfare' is undefined.

evidence.note: OpenAI disclosure (Oct 2026): Microsoft is still its primary cloud partner. Shows continuing support, not withdrawal, and does not settle an indefinite forecast.
Anthropic disclosure (Apr 2026): expanded Google/Broadcom compute and continuing AWS support. Continuing ties only.
Anthropic disclosure (Apr 2026): new Amazon deal and investment. A finite commercial commitment does not resolve eventual withdrawal or establish a subsidy.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. By the cutoff the evidence shows cloud support continuing and expanding for both firms, but no withdrawal and no cessation. Nothing decisive rules out the mechanism. Continued partnerships do not disprove an open-ended forecast, so it stays unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own parenthetical rebuttal of a hype claim.

semantics.note: 'They haven't' is a firm observation. 'Doesn't seem to be a path' is hedged and should not be scored by itself; the proposition keeps the 'seems' hedge.

contract.note: The plain reading (the cost of delivering or using comparable capabilities had not materially fallen) is ordinary, and the period is reasonable. Only the firm 'haven't' clause should decide the outcome; the hedged path clause is not scored on its own.

evidence.note: OpenAI pricing announcement (May 2024): a GPT-4-level model at half GPT-4 Turbo's API price. A material fall in usage cost for comparable capability within the period.
vLLM deployment report (2023): the same serving traffic handled with 50% fewer GPUs, with lower operational costs. A deployed fall in serving cost within the period.

reviews.rationale: Within Jan 2023–Jul 2024, two items document material cost falls for comparable workloads: customer prices halved for GPT-4-level capability, and serving GPUs halved for the same traffic. The firm claim that costs had not come down fails on the contract's plain reading. The hedged path clause is not scored.

semantics.note: Firm observation about the past 18 months. The proposition matches the words.

contract.note: Ed is rebutting the hype that AI will create jobs in the labour-market sense. Reading his words as 'zero gross positions anywhere', so that any AI startup hire disproves them, stretches the claim against him. An informed reader would take it as no meaningful job creation across the economy, which the contract explicitly does not require.

evidence.note: Mistral CEO keynote (Nov 2023) describing a newly founded team. The quoted excerpt does not show the headcount of 18. A startup's staff do not measure job creation across the economy or net job creation.

reviews.rationale: Under the contract's literal gross reading, a staffed new AI startup would contradict the claim. But that reading is unfair to the labour-market sense of the words. Under the ordinary reading, the packet has no employment data on generative AI's job creation for Jan 2023–Jul 2024, so the evidence does not settle the claim.
